newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Pacific Link may see 40 pct profit drop - First Pac.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Link may see 40 pct profit drop - First Pac.

text.p: First Pacific Co Ltd's Hong Kong cellular phone arm Pacific Link Communications Ltd could see a decline in earnings of up to 40 percent in 1997, First Pacific managing director Manuel Pangilinan said on Wednesday.
"I think the decline in earnings will be anywhere between 20 to 40 percent," he told Reuters in an interview, adding that the decline was more likely to be at the higher end of that range.
Pacific Link contributed HK$453 million to First Pacific's profits in 1996
Pangilinan said First Pacific was seeking to restructure the business. "I think we have to given the competitive situation in Hong Kong. Something has got to be done about it."

"There is a range of possibilities - get a strategic partner to help with the operating expertise, marketing expertise, financial capital or you attempt as well to consolidate the industry so there are fewer players," he said.
Pangilinan said a merger was a possibility but he did not think it would happen in the near term.

First Pacific said on Tuesday that the holding company for its telecommunications operations in Asia, Asia Link, was currently in discussions with several parties as part of its efforts to enhance its telecommunications businesses.
Pangilinan said the company would like to bring in a strategic partner, "someone who is marketing oriented and an existing telco operator".
But he declined to say who the company was in discussions with. "I can't be specific. These are big names."
Pangilinan said First Pacific's other telecommunications operations were on track. The whole telecommunications business contributed about 27 percent to 1996 earnings.

"I think it (the contribution) will be held back this year with the decline in earnings of Pacific Link... It might be able to maintain its share of earnings. We had anticipated it to grow as a proportion," Pangilinan said.
"We are tempering our own projections by the year 2000 but it will continue to be a major contributor to the earnings of the group," he added.
